# Otto Flags

> Otto Flags is a feature flag service that AI agents manage over MCP and running apps evaluate through SDKs. If you are an agent wiring an SDK into a project, connect to the MCP endpoint, call `whoami`, then call `sdk_guide` with the project's language.

The server is at https://otto-flags.savvagent.com. Agents manage flags at `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP MCP, OAuth bearer tokens issued by the otto platform). Applications evaluate flags through an SDK over REST at `/api/...` with an app key; the SDK path never goes through the agent surface.

## Start here

- Connect to https://otto-flags.savvagent.com/mcp, call `whoami` to see the organization and your scopes, then call `sdk_guide(language, app?)`. It returns install, initialization and usage steps for that language, filled in with the app's id, name and public client key when `app` is given.
- Every SDK install is pinned to a commit of savvagent/otto-flags. Find one with `git ls-remote https://github.com/savvagent/otto-flags main` and use that SHA where a guide says `<commit>`.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/savvagent/otto-flags/blob/main/AGENTS.md): how an agent finds the right SDK in this repository.
- [SDK developer guide](https://github.com/savvagent/otto-flags/blob/main/docs/SDK-DEVELOPER-GUIDE.md): the REST wire contract every SDK implements.

## MCP tools

- `whoami`: the organization, role and scopes this token opens.
- `usage`: this month's usage meters, the budget and any billing block.
- `list_apps`: the apps (one per codebase or service) that own flags.
- `create_app`: create an app and return its SDK keys (owner or admin).
- `update_app`: rename or change an app's settings.
- `rotate_app_keys`: issue new SDK keys for an app (owner or admin).
- `list_flags`: the flags in an app.
- `get_flag`: one flag with its environments, rules and current version.
- `create_flag`: create a flag, switched off everywhere.
- `update_flag`: change a flag's description, variations or tags.
- `set_flag_environment`: turn a flag on or off per environment, set rollout, targeting and the default variation.
- `archive_flag`: retire a flag.
- `restore_flag`: bring an archived flag back.
- `rollback_flag`: restore a flag's previous version, or any version from its history.
- `flag_history`: every version of a flag and why it changed.
- `evaluate_flag`: what a given user would get, and why, without changing anything.
- `flag_health`: error rate with the flag on versus off, from SDK reports.
- `set_rollback_policy`: arm auto-rollback for a flag in one environment.
- `remove_rollback_policy`: delete a rollback policy.
- `list_rollback_policies`: the policies and whether each is armed.
- `propose_rollback`: a dry run of what auto-rollback would do right now.
- `rollback_events`: what auto-rollback has done.
- `sdk_guide`: the integration guide for one language, filled in for an app.

## SDKs

Each language below is a `sdk_guide` name. The link is the package README.

- `python`: [packages/python-server](https://github.com/savvagent/otto-flags/blob/main/packages/python-server/README.md)

## Quick start (Python)

Install from source, pinned to a commit:

```bash
pip install "otto-flags @ git+https://github.com/savvagent/otto-flags@<commit>#subdirectory=packages/python-server"
```

```python
import os

from otto_flags import FlagClient, FlagClientConfig, FlagContext

client = FlagClient(
    FlagClientConfig(
        api_key=os.environ["OTTO_FLAGS_API_KEY"],
        application_id="<app id from list_apps>",
        defaults={"new-checkout": False},
    )
)

if client.is_enabled("new-checkout", FlagContext(user_id="user-123")):
    ...
```

Keep the server key in the app's secret store, never in code. `sdk_guide` with `language: "python"` and an `app` returns the full guide with the app's id filled in.
